#!/bin/sh
# Start/stop the PS-local Qt HMI.
#
# The application owns the PL sensor DMA ring (/dev/pl_ctrl + /dev/mem), so stop
# sends SIGTERM first: the Qt event loop exits, the window is destroyed and
# pl_dma_ring_stop() writes RING|STOP to DMA_CTRL. SIGKILL is a last resort and
# leaves the ring started. Both branches then verify DMA_CTRL through plctl and
# clear the ring when it is still busy, so the stop result does not depend on the
# application releasing the engine itself.

PIDFILE=/var/run/mlk_ps_local.pid
APP_COMM=mlk_ps_local
TERM_WAIT=5

# /var/run may be missing on a minimal rootfs.
if ! mkdir -p "${PIDFILE%/*}" 2>/dev/null; then
    PIDFILE=/tmp/mlk_ps_local.pid
fi

# Print the pid of the running application: pidfile first, then a /proc comm
# scan so a manually started instance is found as well. BusyBox has no
# pgrep/pkill, so neither is used.
running_pid()
{
    _pid=
    if [ -r "$PIDFILE" ]; then
        read -r _pid < "$PIDFILE"
    fi
    case "$_pid" in
    ''|*[!0-9]*) _pid= ;;
    esac
    if [ -n "$_pid" ] && [ -r "/proc/$_pid/comm" ]; then
        _comm=
        read -r _comm < "/proc/$_pid/comm"
        if [ "$_comm" = "$APP_COMM" ]; then
            echo "$_pid"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    for _dir in /proc/[0-9]*; do
        [ -r "$_dir/comm" ] || continue
        _comm=
        read -r _comm < "$_dir/comm"
        if [ "$_comm" = "$APP_COMM" ]; then
            echo "${_dir#/proc/}"
            return 0
        fi
    done
    return 1
}

start()
{
    [ -x /opt/qt_play/run_arm_app.sh ] || exit 0
    _pid=$(running_pid)
    if [ -n "$_pid" ]; then
        echo "$APP_COMM already running (pid $_pid)"
        return 0
    fi
    rm -f "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null
    # exec keeps one pid across run_arm_app.sh and mlk_ps_local.
    (
        cd /opt/qt_play || exit 1
        exec ./run_arm_app.sh
    ) &
    _pid=$!
    if echo "$_pid" > "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "$APP_COMM started (pid $_pid, pidfile $PIDFILE)"
    else
        echo "$APP_COMM started (pid $_pid); pidfile $PIDFILE not writable" >&2
    fi
}

# Clear a DMA ring the application left started. plctl owns the register
# offsets and bit positions (host/ps-local/driver/pl_ctrl_uapi.h), so the script
# does not repeat them: "ring-stop" issues the graceful STOP and writes
# DMA_CTRL back as 0 even when the application was killed.
clear_ring()
{
    command -v plctl >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
    if plctl ring-stop >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "cleared PL sensor DMA ring"
        return 0
    fi
    # Fallback for a rootfs whose plctl predates ring-stop: DMA_CTRL=0x90,
    # BUSY bit 8, RING bit 3, STOP bit 4 (see pl_ctrl_uapi.h).
    _val=$(plctl read 0x90 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' \r')
    _hex=${_val##*=0x}
    case "$_hex" in
    ''|*[!0-9a-fA-F]*) return 0 ;;
    esac
    if [ "$(( (0x$_hex >> 8) & 1 ))" -eq 1 ]; then
        plctl write 0x90 0x18 >/dev/null 2>&1
        plctl write 0x90 0x0 >/dev/null 2>&1
        echo "cleared PL sensor DMA ring ($(plctl read 0x90 2>/dev/null))"
        return 0
    fi
    if [ "$(( 0x$_hex ))" -ne 0 ]; then
        plctl write 0x90 0x0 >/dev/null 2>&1
        echo "cleared idle DMA control ($(plctl read 0x90 2>/dev/null))"
    fi
    return 0
}

stop()
{
    _pid=$(running_pid)
    if [ -z "$_pid" ]; then
        rm -f "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null
        echo "$APP_COMM not running"
        return 0
    fi
    kill -TERM "$_pid" 2>/dev/null
    _waited=0
    while [ "$_waited" -lt "$TERM_WAIT" ]; do
        if ! kill -0 "$_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
            rm -f "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null
            echo "$APP_COMM stopped (pid $_pid)"
            clear_ring
            return 0
        fi
        sleep 1
        _waited=$((_waited + 1))
    done
    if kill -0 "$_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "$APP_COMM did not exit within ${TERM_WAIT}s; sending SIGKILL (pid $_pid)" >&2
        kill -KILL "$_pid" 2>/dev/null
        _waited=0
        while [ "$_waited" -lt 2 ] && kill -0 "$_pid" 2>/dev/null; do
            sleep 1
            _waited=$((_waited + 1))
        done
        rm -f "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null
        echo "warning: $APP_COMM ignored SIGTERM and was killed (pid $_pid)" >&2
        clear_ring
        return 1
    fi
    rm -f "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null
    echo "$APP_COMM stopped (pid $_pid)"
    clear_ring
    return 0
}

restart()
{
    stop
    start
}

status()
{
    _pid=$(running_pid)
    if [ -n "$_pid" ]; then
        echo "$APP_COMM running (pid $_pid)"
        return 0
    fi
    echo "$APP_COMM not running"
    return 3
}

case "$1" in
  start) start ;;
  stop) stop ;;
  restart) restart ;;
  status) status ;;
  *)
    echo "usage: $0 {start|stop|restart|status}" >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
esac
exit $?
